correctness.rationale: The half-range compression law follows from a genuine infinite argument, not the finite verifier. After the first effective \(a\), the image lies in \(R=\{1,\ldots,n-2\}\). Direct action analysis shows that every word of length at most three is injective on \(R\), while among length-four words only \(b^3a\) creates a collision and it creates exactly one. Hence a further one-state loss costs at least four letters and a two-state loss at least five. Combining these local costs gives the lower bounds \(5k\) and \(5k+1\), while the two displayed periodic words have the claimed disjoint hole sets throughout deficiency \(\le(n+1)/2\). A fresh independent power-set BFS for \(n=5,7,9\) reproduced the initial profiles \((1,1,5)\), \((1,1,5,6)\), and \((1,1,5,6,10)\).
residual_risks: No formula is established beyond deficiency \((n+1)/2\).
